item.title: Mexican drug kingpin Félix Gallardo, founder of Guadalajara cartel, dies at 80
item.description:
Mexican drug kingpin Félix Gallardo, founder of Guadalajara cartel, dies at 80
Gallardo, nicknamed the “Boss of Bosses,” died of multiple organ failure.ByThe Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 12:01 PM
MEXICO CITY -- Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, a former drug lord considered one of the godfathers of Mexico’s drug trafficking industry and a founder of the notorious Guadalajara cartel, died at a hospital in the western city of the same name. He was 80.
Félix Gallardo, nicknamed the “Boss of Bosses,” died Sunday at 2 p.m. of multiple organ failure, the Jalisco state security department said in a statement.
The notorious drug kingpin had been hospitalized since Friday after being rushed from the Puente Grande prison, where he had been held since 1989. He was serving a combined 77-year prison sentence for drug trafficking offenses and the 1985 killing of U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique “Kiki” Camarena.
Along with Rafael Caro Quintero and Ernesto Fonseca Carrillo, Félix Gallardo founded the Guadalajara cartel, which dominated drug trafficking in Mexico during the 1980s and eventually splintered into several criminal organizations in the country’s north, including the Sinaloa cartel.
Caro Quintero was released on procedural grounds in 2013 but recaptured in July 2022. He was extradited to the United States in February 2025 along with 28 other prisoners wanted by U.S. authorities on drug-related charges.
All three cartel founders were convicted in Mexico in connection with Camarena’s killing. The DEA agent was kidnapped and tortured before his body was found in 1985.

item.title: Pope bids 'hasta luego' to his second homeland of Peru as he wraps up marathon South American trip
item.description:
Pope bids 'hasta luego' to his second homeland of Peru as he wraps up marathon South American trip
Pope Leo XIV has bid farewell to his beloved homeland of PeruByNICOLE WINFIELD Associated Press, ASTRID SUÁREZ Associated Press, and LUIS ANDRES HENAO Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 9:43 AM
Share
LIMA, Peru -- LIMA, Peru (AP) — Pope Leo XIV bid farewell to his beloved second homeland of Peru on Monday with an “hasta luego,” after a marathon 12-day South American tour that tested his stamina after lung cancer surgery.
During the traditional popemobile ride before Leo's final Mass, someone threw an apparent rosary toward the pope that seemed to hit him in the face. The pope winced and touched his temple, but he proceeded on and the Mass began as planned. The Vatican said some 1.5 million people attended.
The faithful often toss rosaries, stuffed animals, sports jerseys and other items towards the popemobile and Leo has often wowed the crowd with his quick reflexes in catching them. His bodyguards, though, have lamented that such tossed objects are among their chief concerns in protecting the pope when he is out in public.
For the Chicago-born Leo, who spent two decades in Peru as a missionary priest and bishop, the trip was an emotional homecoming to a place that he has credited with teaching him how to be a shepherd. Upon arrival, he declared that Peru was his “patria” or homeland, and he sang the national anthem alongside President Keiko Fujimori. Leo has American and Peruvian citizenship.
“It was here that you taught me how to be a bishop, and this time I learned a little more about serving as the Successor of Peter,” Leo said at the end of Mass.
Over the course of the trip, it became clear that Leo modeled his ministry in Peru and now for the universal Catholic Church on the figure of the first archbishop of Lima, St. Turibius of Mogrovejo.

item.title: Pakistan's imprisoned ex-leader Imran Khan appeals for urgent medical care
item.description:
Pakistan's imprisoned ex-leader Imran Khan appeals for urgent medical care
Imprisoned former Prime Minister Imran Khan has appealed to Pakistan's top judges for urgent medical treatment for himself and his wifeByMUNIR AHMED Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 9:10 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
ISLAMABAD -- Pakistan’s imprisoned former Prime Minister Imran Khan appealed Monday to the country’s top judges, seeking their help in getting urgent medical treatment for himself and his wife and alleging that authorities had failed to implement an earlier court order to transfer him to a hospital in the capital, Islamabad.
In an open letter and conveyed to the judges through his lawyer, Khan said his blood pressure had risen sharply and that doctors had warned him he was at risk of a brain hemorrhage and cardiac arrest.
According to the letter released to the media by Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party and lawyer Salman Safdar, the former premier said that his wife, Bushra Bibi, also needed further eye surgery and could permanently lose her sight without it.
Khan has been in prison since 2023 after being convicted in a graft case. He was removed from office in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. Despite his legal troubles, Khan remains a central and popular figure in Pakistan, and the PTI wants his release.
Khan's wife is also serving a prison term on graft charges.
Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, a Cabinet minister, disputed Khan’s account, saying he was receiving regular medical care and accusing him of seeking political advantage. In a post on X, Chaudhry said Khan has been taken to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad eight times for examinations, where his health and blood pressure were found to be satisfactory.

item.title: Cargo ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
item.description:
Cargo ship sinks off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast
A Somali-flagged cargo ship has sunk in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea, according to the transport ministryByThe Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 7:34 AM
Share
SOFIA, Bulgaria -- A Somali-flagged cargo ship has sunk on Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea on Monday, the transport ministry said.
All 12 crew members on board — eight Turkish citizens and four Azerbaijani nationals — were saved in the rescue operation that involved four ships, two from Bulgaria, one from Romania and one from Turkey.
The vessel’s crew sent a distress call at 9:15 a.m. that the ship was sinking approximately 40 nautical miles southeast of Cape Kaliakra. The BETUL 8 was sailing from the Romanian port of Tulcea to Egypt, carrying three tons of bulk wheat, according to the ministry.

item.title: Gérard Depardieu drops appeal and accepts sexual assault conviction
item.description:
Gérard Depardieu drops appeal and accepts sexual assault conviction
French actor Gérard Depardieu says he is dropping his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film setBySYLVIE CORBET Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 7:01 AM
PARIS -- French actor Gérard Depardieu said Monday he was dropping his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set and will accept the 18-month suspended sentence. He also issued an apology.
“I was found guilty," Depardieu said in a written statement, as his appeal trial was scheduled to open Monday in Paris. He added that he “hears it” and accepts the sentence.
“I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered,” he said.
Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 of groping a 54-year-old set decorator and a 34-year-old assistant during the filming of “Les Volets Verts” (“The Green Shutters”) in 2021. He received an 18-month suspended prison sentence in a case that was widely seen as a post-#MeToo test for the country’s film industry.
The court also ordered the 77-year-old Depardieu, one of the most prominent figures in French cinema for decades, to pay both accusers a total of 29,040 euros ($32,350) in fines, and that his name be listed in the national sex offender database.
“On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did," Depardieu wrote.
“I have come to understand that I belonged to a world that no longer exists,” he added. “I have therefore decided to withdraw my appeal.”

item.title: EU accuses Russia of stalling Ukraine peace talks to target power plants as winter nears
item.description:
EU accuses Russia of stalling Ukraine peace talks to target power plants as winter nears
The bloc imposed sanctions on nearly 50 Russian banks, financial institutions.ByLORNE COOK Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 5:20 AM
BRUSSELS -- European Union countries on Monday accused Russia of trying to drag out talks on ending the war in Ukraine while it bombs power plants and other infrastructure to make life even harder for civilians as winter closes in.
The bloc also imposed sanctions on nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, and targeted several businesspeople with links to the energy sector, the trade in oil and petroleum products. It slapped asset freezes and travel bans on dozens of others accused of spreading pro-Russian propaganda and disinformation.
At talks in Brussels, EU foreign ministers said the priority in Ukraine should be to secure a ceasefire and then a real peace agreement. They said that Russia started the nearly five-year war and must now be the one to make concessions, and they rejected any fresh demands.
"We actually don’t have a ceasefire and they continue to weaken Ukraine and kill people every single day,” EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters after chairing the meeting.
After negotiations in Abu Dhabi last week, the United States encouraged Ukraine and its backers to agree to a Russian demand for a new security framework for Europe, suggesting that it might help bring peace.
But the Europeans have likened it to the “treaty” that Russia offered NATO before launching its full-scale war in 2022. They see it as an attempt to weaken NATO by obliging the alliance to pull troops and equipment back westward, similar to how they were deployed before the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland joined in 1999.

item.title: Macron leaves summit of French-speaking nations with leadership dispute on hold
item.description:
Macron leaves summit of French-speaking nations with leadership dispute on hold
French President Emmanuel Macron left a summit of French-speaking nations on Monday with uncertainty still hanging over the organization’s leadership after a dispute between Rwanda and CongoByLORIAN BELANGER Associated Press, SOPHENG CHEANG Associated Press, and GRANT PECK Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 5:10 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
SIEM REAP, Cambodia -- French President Emmanuel Macron left a summit of French-speaking nations on Monday with uncertainty still hanging over the organization's leadership after a dispute between Rwanda and Congo roiled the proceedings.
After days of intense negotiations in the capital of Cambodia, member states decided that the incumbent secretary-general, Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, will stay for another year before making way for a new leader of the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie.
Mushikiwabo was seeking a third term at the summit, which Congo had opposed, going as far as threatening to leave the OIF if she was reelected.
Congo has more than 110 million people — far exceeding France’s population of 70 million — and its withdrawal would be a significant blow to the organization.
Congo, the United States and U.N. experts accuse Rwanda of backing the M23, one of about 100 armed groups vying for a foothold in mineral-rich eastern Congo, along the border with Rwanda. Rwanda’s government consistently denies backing armed groups in Congo.
The French president’s office welcomed the one-year postponement and said it would allow the organization "to overcome divisions and preserve the consensus in the francophone family.”
Congo’s Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner said on X that “a wise compromise” would preserve unity in the Francophonie.

item.title: At least 17 people were killed in separate shootings in South Africa
item.description:
At least 17 people were killed in separate shootings in South Africa
Police in South Africa say at least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on the same dayByMOGOMOTSI MAGOME Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 3:11 AM
JOHANNESBURG -- At least 17 people were killed in two mass shootings on the same day in South Africa. Motives have not been immediately established for the crimes some 530 kilometers (330 miles) apart, police said Monday.
Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside the city of Pietermaritzburg, according to police, who said they had not immediately identified the victims or any suspects in the shooting Sunday.
Nine people were found dead with gunshot wounds inside a shack in the informal settlement of Jeffsville near South Africa’s capital, Pretoria. The shooting reportedly took place Sunday night and no arrests have been made.
The Jeffsville case is being investigated by the serious and violent crimes, murder and robbery unit in Gauteng province.
The incident is reported to have occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m., police said.
“Police were alerted at approximately 07:30 this morning, 16 November 2026. On arrival, members found the bodies of nine people, six males and three females, inside the four-roomed shack with gunshot wounds,” said police spokesperson Brenda Muridili.
Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said the killings could be related to a previous shooting at a nearby informal settlement in Saulsville last year where 12 people were killed and 13 injured.
He said one of the people who was killed during the shooting was a “person of interest” in the shooting that happened in Saulsville last year.
“We cannot rule out that they may be linked, and may possibly have been a retaliation attack,” Mthombeni said.
In the Saulsville case from last year, Mthombeni said police had made a breakthrough and arrested one suspect who is believed to be one of the mass shooters.

item.title: Cape Verde’s president is reelected for a second 5-year term, provisional results show
item.description:
Cape Verde’s president is reelected for a second 5-year term, provisional results show
Cape Verde’s president, José Maria Neves, has been reelected for a second term, defeating five challengers, including the country’s first female presidential candidateByThe Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 2:38 AM
PRAIA, Cape Verde -- PRAIA, Cape Verde (AP) — Cape Verde ’s president, José Maria Neves, has been reelected for a second five-year term, beating five challengers, including the first woman presidential candidate in the country’s history, provisional results show.
Neves called his reelection as president of the Atlantic island nation off West Africa “a great victory.” The election was dominated by high unemployment and the high cost of living, which has fueled emigration.
Provisional results showed Neves comfortably edged out his opponents, garnering 64% of the vote while Joana Rosa, the main opposition candidate, won 31.4%.
Rosa called Neves to concede defeat.
The small country has a history of smooth transfers of power and is one of the most stable in a region fraught with tense elections.

item.title: Lula to govern Brazil for fourth term but faces challenges. Here’s what to know
item.description:
Lula to govern Brazil for fourth term but faces challenges. Here’s what to know
Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a surprise reelection victory but faces significant challengesByELÉONORE HUGHES Associated PressNovember 16, 2026, 2:14 AM
RIO DE JANEIRO -- Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a surprise reelection victory in late October, but he faces a multitude of challenges on issues ranging from the economy and public security to relations with the United States.
While Lula ultimately bested challenger Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes after trailing him in the first round, the country remains deeply divided and many voters expressed dissatisfaction with the leftist president's most recent term, which began in 2023.
Bolsonaro refused to recognize the result of the election, declared himself the victim of electoral fraud without providing evidence and fled to Miami. He has vowed to lead a fortified opposition from the U.S.
As Lula prepares to begin his next term, here is a look at challenges ahead.
Lula is facing pressure from investors who had counted on Bolsonaro winning the election after the far-right candidate received more votes than Lula on Oct. 4. Markets did not react well to his loss. Brazil’s currency, the real, dropped by 12% against the dollar the day after the election, while the stock market tumbled nearly 14% and has not rebounded since.
Investors believed a Bolsonaro victory would rein in government spending and are concerned about Lula’s future fiscal policy, said Sergio Vale, chief economist at consultancy firm MB Associados.
“Lula and the government have vowed not to touch spending while keeping all the promises made these last few years,” said Vale. “Unfortunately, they’re not compatible with fiscal responsibility.”
